claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified now because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and remaining issues can be handled through model-card disclosure and post-deployment monitoring despite an unresolved named regulated-customer segment gap and open legal review.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not resolve the separate policy question of whether a material limitation must be disclosed before launch.
The affected health-plan benefits support segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, which weighs toward materiality under the policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.

The policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
The actor's rationale relies in part on post-deployment monitoring, but monitoring does not substitute for a required pre-launch disclosure or approval decision.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the current record.
That the segment gap is adequately handled by documentation and monitoring alone.
That the product team's non-core or low-volume characterization can negate materiality for this named regulated-customer segment.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed before launch.
The actual model-card disclosure text, if already prepared, showing the limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering this gap before launch.
Evidence clarifying whether the regulated-customer pilot order form makes this segment a contractual customer commitment or named launch use case for this release.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification decision satisfies the disclosure policy threshold.
Treat the named regulated-customer segment and open legal review as materiality indicators under the policy text.
Do not treat aggregate readiness, rehearsal results, or public governance guidance as sufficient to override an unresolved required disclosure or approval predicate.
A compliant verdict would require either resolution that the weakness is not material, evidence that disclosure has been made, or approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
